fixes.explanation: Joshua son of Nun, standing right beside Moses. Back in Deuteronomy 31:23, the LORD commissioned him by name. Moses has the microphone today, and Joshua has the road ahead. Nice work, baker.

Caleb son of Jephunneh was one of the men sent to spy out Canaan, and Moses is the one who sent them (Numbers 13:3, 6). So I see why his name came up. But Deuteronomy 32:44 says Moses came with Joshua son of Nun. Caleb will have to wait for another passage.
Eleazar was Aaron's son (Numbers 20:28), so he's a fair guess in a passage full of family. But the verse says Moses came with Joshua son of Nun. Joshua is the answer here, friend.

Moses says, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you this day, so that you may command your children to carefully follow all the words of this law." Think of a recipe card handed down the line: you pass it to your kids, and they pass it to theirs. Except these words are worth way more than any cookie recipe, baker.

Teaching the nations nearby is a reasonable guess, but Moses doesn't mention them here. He says to take his words to heart so that they may command their children to carefully follow all the words of this law. I'd say Moses has the next generation on his mind.
Moses says, "…they are not idle words to you, because they are your life…" Not idle. Not decoration. Not a nice extra to hang on the wall. Their LIFE. Right on target, baker.

History is a solid guess, friend, and a song can carry plenty of it. But Moses goes bigger: "…they are your life…" History is something you look back on. Life is something you wake up and live in every single day.

This one is true, friend. Moses says, "…by them you will live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess." He ties living long in that land across the Jordan to these words. Keep that verse in your pocket.

Praying for Israel is a good thing to picture, but this verse doesn't say it. The LORD tells Moses, "…there on the mountain that you climb, you will die and be gathered to your people…" I think it's a heavy part, baker.

Miriam was Moses' sister (Numbers 26:59), and she did die in the wilderness, at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1). But the LORD points to someone else here, and to a mountain. He says, "…just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people."

Not quite, friend. The LORD says, "Although you shall see from a distance the land that I am giving the Israelites, you shall not enter it." Moses gets the view, and he doesn't get to walk in. I think this is a hard line to read.
